name: Jones

alpha.desc: The front oblique shows a large rural desert parcel with scattered juniper/pinon trees densely surrounding the central structures|The tennis court is visible in the upper-center area|The residence and associated structures are set back significantly from the road, surrounded by a sea of native desert vegetation|The driveway approach through the trees is narrow and winding, with limited cleared width on either side.

bravo.desc: The right-side oblique confirms dense tree coverage along the right flank of the property|The main residence and garage cluster are visible mid-parcel|The gravel area and driveway loop are partially visible through the tree canopy|No cleared staging area is apparent on the right side; vegetation presses close to the structures.

charlie.desc: The rear oblique shows the back of the property is dominated by dense native scrub vegetation and scattered trees with no improved access or cleared area visible|The tennis court structure is faintly visible at upper right|The rear of the residence has no visible road or emergency access route; terrain appears open desert with no fencing or cleared perimeter along the back.

delta.desc: The left-side oblique shows the driveway curving up from the lower left toward the residence, with trees and shrubs lining both sides of the approach|The tennis court and pool/court structure are visible in the upper portion|The curved driveway narrows as it approaches the structures, and trees crowd the corridor throughout|A gravel area near the main structure provides limited turnaround space.

considerations: This is a large rural residential property with a single winding driveway access point off Macalpine Loop. The driveway is curved and tree-lined, limiting visibility and width for apparatus. Dense native juniper/pinon vegetation surrounds the structures on all sides, with no improved rear or side access. The gravel area near the residence provides limited turnaround space but may not accommodate large fire apparatus. The tennis court occupies significant space in the front yard area but is not usable as a staging area. The open perimeter on the rear and sides means there is no fencing barrier but also no cleared defensible corridor for wildfire operations. The property sits in classic WUI (wildland-urban interface) terrain with scattered and clustered trees throughout.
clarifications: Confirm whether the curved driveway can accommodate a full-size fire apparatus (ladder truck or engine) through its entire length. Verify if any secondary emergency access track exists on the rear or sides of the parcel not visible from aerial imagery. Confirm the nature and depth of the gravel area near the residence for use as an apparatus turnaround or staging area. Confirm whether the fence element is a full perimeter fence or a partial yard enclosure, and whether any gates restrict driveway access.
